samples: This program reads numbers from the command line, skips any argument that isn't a valid number (printing a note about each one), and then prints the mean, median and population standard deviation of the rest, rounded to three decimals. If no valid numbers are given, each statistic is reported as "no data". It only needs console and environment access, so it does no file or network work and is safe to run for quick calculations.

This program reads numbers from the command line, skips (and reports) any arguments that aren't valid numbers, and prints their mean, median and population standard deviation, rounded to three decimal places, or "no data" if no valid numbers were given. It only needs console and environment access, so it can't touch files or the network. The statistics functions are also public, so other modules can reuse them, and each returns nothing for an empty list instead of failing.

This program reads numbers from the command line, skips (and reports) any argument that isn't a valid number, and prints the mean, median and population standard deviation of the rest, showing "no data" for each statistic if no numbers were given. Results are rounded to three decimal places. It only needs console and environment access, so it does no file or network I/O, and it's a simple, safe choice if you want quick descriptive statistics from a shell.
